::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Prove $\sin^6x = \frac1{32}(10 − 15\cos2x + 6\cos4x − \cos6x)$](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1703110/prove-sin6x-frac13210-%e2%88%92-15-cos2x-6-cos4x-%e2%88%92-cos6x), asked by [Zero Cipher](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/323979/zero-cipher) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-03-18; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Im trying to prove the following equation:
>
> $$\sin^6x = \frac1{32}(10 − 15\cos2x + 6\cos4x − \cos6x)$$
>
> I have tried to do it several times now but get stuck at different places. I don't know if it's a calculation error or the question is defective. It would be really helpful if someone could point out the method.
>
> we are to use $$z - \frac1{z} = 2i\sin x$$
> $$z^n + (\frac1{z})^n = 2\cos nx$$
:::

[Wolfram Alpha][1] corroborates the identity so I think the question is not defective.  You probably want to apply the identities
$$\begin{align*}
    \sin^2(\theta) &= \frac{1}{2}\left(1-\cos 2\theta\right) \\
    \cos^2(\theta) &= \frac{1}{2}\left(1+\cos 2\theta\right)
\end{align*}$$
several times.


  [1]: http://www.wolframalpha.com/input/?t=crmtb01&f=ob&i=sin%5E6(x)
